newsitem.title: UK: UK gilts recoil from new all-time high, end lower.
newsitem.headline: UK gilts recoil from new all-time high, end lower.

text.p: 1622 GMT - UK gilts reversed a healthy rally which took them to new all-time highs earlier, dipping into negative ground at Monday's close as profit takers cashed in on recent strength. * March gilts down 10/32 at 112-29, back off new 113-15 high * March short stg ends 0.02 lower at 93.70
The future hit a new all-time high early in the session after record low producer prices data for January confirmed pipeline inflationary pressures were being kept under control.

Analysts said the data, showing output prices rose just 1.5 percent year-on-year -- the lowest growth rate for 10 years -- strengthened Chancellor Kenneth Clarke's argument for keeping interest rates steady.
"The PPI numbers give more power to the Chancellor's elbow and clearly support his decision not to tighten last week," said Jeremy Hawkins at Bank of America.
He said the news would be welcomed in the gilt market.
The rally to an all-time high in March gilt futures confirmed this view, but later prompted a bout of selling as investors sought to cash in on recent strength.
Gilts outclassed core European debt markets last week, narrowing the 10-year yield gap to Bunds by around 20 basis points to close at 163 on Friday.

Monday's late turnaround pushed that gap back out to 167 basis points. But players said there was still value to be had. "It is really just a bit of profit taking," said Beauchamp. "I still think gilts are a good buy -- and this is the place to buy them."
With a heavy flow of data ahead, analysts said the gilt market will remain edgy, but should come out on top at the end of the week.
The market must digest the Bank of England's inflation report and January unemoplyment figures on Wednesday and January retail price inflation data on Thursday.
Hawkins said the jobs data would be key.

"The big risk to UK inflation is the labour market and wages," he said. "Non-labour costs are clearly not an issue at the moment, but the risks are high that the rapid pace at which unemployment is falling will force up wages."
The Reuters consensus forecast is for a 30,000 decline in unemployment in January, compared with a hefty 45,000 fall in December.
At the short end of the market, March short sterling futures ended the session 0.02 weaker at 93.70.
